notes: Summary: Enterprise Dedicated evaluation focused on firm SLA guarantees. Sentinel is a EU-headquartered financial data provider building customer-facing chat and search over sensitive docs. They ran a 2-week POC and now in procurement; main negotiation points are uptime %, credit schedule, maintenance windows, and support response times. Key asks: 1) Target uptime 99.95% (they push for 99.99% for critical paths) and tied credit schedule (tiered credits at monthly thresholds); 2) Scheduled maintenance limited to monthly 02:00-04:00 CET or emergency only, advance notice >=72h; 3) Support SLAs: Sev1 initial response 15m, 1hr mitigation window for critical production outages; 4) Reserved GPU planning: baseline commitment ~8 H100-equivalent slots (hot standby across zones) with clear burst policy and cold-warm scaling costs; 5) Data controls: EU-only residency for embeddings + keys bridged to their KMS, SOC2 Type II report and audit logging mandatory. Quote from CTO: "We need financial predictability if an outage costs us revenue — credits and escalation path must be iron-clad." Legal concerns: indemnity/liability cap language and force majeure carve-outs. Action items: draft counter-SLA with explicit credit schedule (example: monthly availability <99.95% = 10% credit, <99.9% = 25%, <99% = 50%; annual cap 100% monthly credits), define maintenance window default + opt-out for critical SLAs, include escalation matrix with named on-call and 15m page for Sev1. POC notes: embeddings throughput target 1200 qps (50ms avg), chat throughput bursts to 400 reqs/min, preference for quantized model variant for cost. Pricing/contract: aiming for $300k-$600k ARR reserved capacity + premium for EU private control plane. Blockers listed in metadata. Supporting artifacts: pricing deck + security FAQ (drive links), legal threads (gmail).
